In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[graph theory]], the '''Wagner graph''' is a 3-[[regular graph]] with 8 [[Vertex (graph theory)|vertices]] and 12 edges.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bondy |first1=J. A. |author-link1=John Adrian Bondy |last2=Murty |first2=U. S. R. |author-link2=U. S. R. Murty |year=2007 |title=Graph Theory |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-1-84628-969-9 |pages=275–276}}</ref> It is the 8-vertex [[Möbius ladder]] graph.

==Properties==
As a Möbius ladder, the Wagner graph is [[Planar graph|nonplanar]] but has [[Crossing number (graph theory)|crossing number]] one, making it an [[apex graph]]. It can be embedded without crossings on a [[torus]] or [[projective plane]], so it is also a [[toroidal graph]]. It has girth 4, diameter 2, radius 2, [[chromatic number]] 3, [[chromatic index]] 3 and is both 3-[[k-vertex-connected graph|vertex-connected]] and 3-[[k-edge-connected graph|edge-connected]].

The Wagner graph has 392 [[spanning tree]]s; it and the [[complete bipartite graph]] {{math|''K''{{sub|3,3}}}} have the most spanning trees among all cubic graphs with the same number of vertices.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Jakobson |first1=Dmitry |last2=Rivin |first2=Igor |year=1999 |title=On some extremal problems in graph theory |eprint=math.CO/9907050 }}</ref>

The Wagner graph is a [[vertex-transitive graph]] but is not [[edge-transitive graph|edge-transitive]]. Its full automorphism group is isomorphic to the [[dihedral group]] {{math|D{{sub|8}}}} of order 16, the group of symmetries of an [[octagon]], including both rotations and reflections.

The [[characteristic polynomial]] of the Wagner graph is
:<math>(x-3)(x-1)^2(x+1)(x^2+2x-1)^2.</math>
It is the only graph with this characteristic polynomial, making it a graph determined by its [[Spectral graph theory|spectrum]].

The Wagner graph is [[triangle-free graph|triangle-free]] and has [[independence number]] three, providing one half of the proof that the [[Ramsey number]] {{math|''R''(3,4)}} (the least number {{mvar|n}} such that any {{mvar|n}}-vertex graph contains either a triangle or a four-vertex independent set) is&nbsp;9.<ref>{{cite book |last=Soifer |first=Alexander |year=2008 |title=The Mathematical Coloring Book |title-link=The Mathematical Coloring Book |publisher=Springer-Verlag |isbn=978-0-387-74640-1 |page=245}}</ref>

==Graph minors==
Möbius ladders play an important role in the theory of [[graph minor]]s. The earliest result of this type is a 1937 theorem of [[Klaus Wagner]] (part of a cluster of results known as [[Wagner's theorem]]) that graphs with no ''K''<sub>5</sub> minor can be formed by using [[clique-sum]] operations to combine planar graphs and the Möbius ladder ''M''<sub>8</sub>.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Wagner |first=K. |authorlink=Klaus Wagner |year=1937 |title=Über eine Eigenschaft der ebenen Komplexe |language=German |journal=Mathematische Annalen |doi=10.1007/BF01594196 |s2cid=123534907 |volume=114 |issue=1 |pages=570–590}}</ref> For this reason ''M''<sub>8</sub> is called the Wagner graph.

The Wagner graph is also one of four minimal [[forbidden minor]]s for the graphs of [[treewidth]] at most three (the other three being the [[complete graph]] ''K''<sub>5</sub>, the graph of the [[regular octahedron]], and the graph of the [[pentagonal prism]]) and one of four minimal forbidden minors for the graphs of [[branchwidth]] at most three (the other three being ''K''<sub>5</sub>, the graph of the octahedron, and the [[hypercube graph|cube graph]]).<ref>{{cite journal |last=Bodlaender |first=Hans L. |authorlink=Hans L. Bodlaender |year=1998 |title=A partial ''k''-arboretum of graphs with bounded treewidth |journal=Theoretical Computer Science |doi=10.1016/S0304-3975(97)00228-4 |hdl=1874/18312 |hdl-access=free |volume=209 |issue=1–2 |pages=1–45}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bodlaender |first1=Hans L. |author-link1=Hans L. Bodlaender |last2=Thilikos |first2=Dimitrios M. |year=1999 |title=Graphs with branchwidth at most three |journal=Journal of Algorithms |doi=10.1006/jagm.1999.1011 |hdl=1874/2734 |hdl-access=free |volume=32 |issue=2 |pages=167–194}}</ref>

==Construction==
The Wagner graph is a [[cubic graph|cubic]] [[Hamiltonian graph]] and can be defined by the [[LCF notation]] [4]<sup>8</sup>. It is an instance of an [[Andrásfai graph]], a type of [[circulant graph]] in which the vertices can be arranged in a cycle and each vertex is connected to the other vertices whose positions differ by a number that is 1 (mod 3).
It is also isomorphic to the [[circular clique]] {{math|''K''<sub>8/3</sub>}}.

It can be drawn as a [[ladder graph]] with 4 rungs made cyclic on a topological [[Möbius strip]].
